etymologies.etymologyHTML: From LASER, acronym of light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation Coined by American physicist Gordon Gould in 1957. Originally called an optical maser.

definitions.definition: A device that produces a monochromatic, coherent beam of light.
A beam of light produced by such a device; a laser beam.

quote.citation: 2004 May 18, PC Mag, volume 23, number 9, page 117:
quote.text: The bad news is that nearly every color laser is too big to share a desk with comfortably.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, medicine) Ellipsis of laser hair removal.
(transitive) To cut, destroy or treat with a laser.
(sports, informal, transitive) To throw or kick with laser-like precision.

quote.citation: 2009 February 2, Dave Perkins, “Steelers tiptoe past Cards”, in Toronto Star‎[1]:
quote.text: None was any more sensational than No.6, a fantastic 27-23 last-gasp win over the Arizona Cardinals, cemented by a brilliant toe-sticking TD catch by Santonio Holmes in the back of the end zone with 35 seconds remaining on a pass lasered by quarterback Ben Roethlisberger.

definitions.definition: A gum resin obtained from certain umbelliferous plants.
